<div class="no-left-nav"></div>

The Onboarding Track is for projects that are ready to move from idea to an actual Civic Tech DC Project.

The first step is to meet our team in person by attending a project night. We highly recommend reaching out to us at [team@civictechdc.org](mailto:team@civictechdc.org) beforehand with a summary of your idea and what you hope to accomplish. That way, we can prepare for your arrival as project nights tend to get very busy. If you can’t attend in person, you can also request a virtual conversation.

**Note:** we may recommend your project join the Incubator Track if it's not ready according to our criteria.

---

## 1. Process

You do not need a polished pitch when you first meet. It’s okay to bring early ideas and what matters most is having a clear understanding of:

- **The problem:** What are you trying to solve?
- **The people:** Who experiences this problem?
- **The idea:** What might you build or explore?
- **The goal:** What would a useful first milestone look like?
- **The commitment:** How much time can you realistically put into leading the project?

We’ll ask questions (probably a lot) to understand the idea and identify what support you might need.

## 2. Review period

After the initial conversation, the team will review your project internally to confirm alignment with our project criteria. This typically takes about **one week**. In some cases, we may also confirm alignment during Project Night and invite you to give a short 30-second intro at the end of the night.

During this time, we may follow up with clarifying questions or suggestions to help refine your idea.

## 3. Confirmation & Next Steps

Once approved, we’ll invite you to officially launch your project. At this point, you’ll move from the Incubator Track into Project Setup, where you’ll define the project, prepare the repository, and get ready to bring in contributors.
